title: Check your understanding: SSH Configuration for Git

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of ssh configuration for git?
options: SSH remotes rely on configured keys and server host verification. A successful authentication test does not eliminate the need to protect private keys and follow the organization’s key lifecycle policy.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: SSH remotes rely on configured keys and server host verification. A successful authentication test does not eliminate the need to protect private keys and follow the organization’s key lifecycle policy.
questions.explanation: SSH remotes rely on configured keys and server host verification. A successful authentication test does not eliminate the need to protect private keys and follow the organization’s key lifecycle policy.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git config --show-origin --get core.sshCommand` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with ssh configuration for git?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
